newsitem.title: UK: UK firms still using cash for capital purchases.
newsitem.headline: UK firms still using cash for capital purchases.

text.p: UK companies, including those in the finance sector who advocate tax-efficient long-term funding, are still using cash to fund capital purchases, according to a survey by asset finance company Barclays Mercantile.

"The finance sector is not practising what it preaches," said a note with the poll. "Although 84 percent of those questioned had invested in IT equipment over the last year, 87 percent used cash rather than long-term funding."

The poll, based on 204 interviews in June, found that the use of cash increased with the size of the company -- under half of small companies polled relied on their own funds to acquire necessary plant and equipment, but nearly 70 percent of larger corporates used cash.
Less than a quarter of those questioned plan major acquisitions up to two years ahead and only nine percent plan up to five years ahead.
Barclays Mercantile said that the Scottish companies questioned had "the most healthy attitude to funding".
"Sixty percent use long-term leasing or hire purchase agreements for major purchases. Scottish directors also plan ahead -- 24 percent are looking five years in the future."
